tutorial.title: Synchrony and Asynchrony in JS
tutorial.descriptionContent: Challenges are more difficult exercises that will test your skills.

executableContent.instructions:
It's level prep time! We don't have enough supplies for the next quest, so we must visit the in-game shop with a list. Write a program that prints the items we need.

1. Use the `.map()` method on the `itemsArray` and save it into `newArrayOfStrings` .
2. Use `shopList` for the callback function of `.map()`.

files.name: script.js

executableContent.instructions:
A game designer wants to award bonus loot to the two strongest heroes in the party. The designer knows the strongest two heroes have more than 4/5 health potions in their inventory. Help the designer identify the best two potion counts by calling the callback function.

1. Include in `bestPotions` the `potionCounts` array with the `.filter()` method.
2. Pass the `callbackConditional` function to the `.filter()` method to return the best two potion counts from the `potionCounts` array.

executableContent.instructions:
We need to test a tiny game function that adds points to a player score. The function takes two point values and a callback.

1. Include `5` and `7` and the callback function as parameters to the `addScore` function to see if it works.

executableContent.instructions:
We want to create a small game log that shows two messages. The second message should appear 1.5 seconds after the first one.

1. Add a `setTimeout` that calls the `spawnEnemy` function after 1.5 seconds.

executableContent.instructions:
This program checks if the player has enough health potions for the next level.
1. Add code that resolves with the message `"You have enough potions for the party."`.
2. When there are few potions, create the reject scenario that prints `We need more potions`.

It is time to power up our player, and we want to add two health potions.
1. Add `async` and `await` to enable the asynchronous response of the functions inside `healMyPlayer`.
